reason: The registry of dynamic packages and the node:vm host half become a plugin host component that runs each plugin as a confined, supervised process whose contributions are effects of its fiber; the inspect registry half moves to the inspect component. Nothing is evaluated inside the host.

It evaluates a plugin's browser half inside the page and mounts it through the client loader; the Go UI is rendered by the host and has no client plugin runtime, and a plugin contributes no UI in protocol version 1. 83 percent of its source is two generated catalogues of the React slot surface.

The read-only inspection tool is kept as harness_inspect over host-only providers that read live registries and schemas derived from Go types; 98.1 percent of the upstream source (879,589 of 896,186 bytes) is a generated catalogue of in-process APIs that a plugin process cannot call, so it is replaced by a provider that serves the plugin protocol itself.

The panel's rows become rows of the server-rendered plugins page built from the plugin descriptor, its approve and decline controls become area A17's consent fragment, and the cards for cordis_define, cordis_run, stop and undefine have no tools left to render; an attach is shown as a transcript notice from its own logged event.

No page loads code or reports a resolution: enabling a model-written plugin is one consent item in the host's interaction registry that settles exactly once by compare-and-swap, and what runs is fixed by a digest, so there is no stale success to refuse and nothing to retry.

The limit describes a JavaScript client plugin waiting for a Remote namespace it declares in its inject list; the Go design has no client-side plugin or loader in the browser (DH-ADR-3), so there is nothing to park.

Slot admission is a property of the React client's slot registry, which exists only because the upstream client is a JavaScript plugin runtime; a Go plugin contributes no UI, and what it may contribute is carried by the manifest's capability list.

The two hand-mirrored whitelists become one capability table in the contract package; the gate, the generated protocol schema, the operator's display and the PluginProtocol inspect provider all read that one table, and a test enumerates it.

The gap between a load receipt and a later React render exists only because a browser half renders in the page after loading; a Go plugin renders nothing, and its readiness is the handshake plus the first tool listing.

No plugin needs a page to run. An attach asks one consent through the interaction registry, and where no answerer is bound (headless, ACP automation) it is refused at once as plugin/consent-unavailable instead of suspending; installed plugins hold standing grants and ask nothing.

Unattended automation uses installed plugins, whose grants an owner recorded beforehand, so no request waits for a person; an attach with nobody to ask fails closed immediately, and one with an answerer is bounded by the asking tool call's deadline and cancellation.

The timeout no longer bounds a synchronous slice of a script in the host's own thread: a plugin is an operating-system process with a start-up deadline, a per-call deadline from the pipeline, a ping deadline and a stop ladder that ends in killing the process tree.

There is one authority, the host, and one identity for what runs, the digest recorded at approval; no second party reports a revision that the registry can have moved past, so a request cannot be left suspended by a refused answer.

What a plugin asks for is declared in its manifest and read by Inspect before anything runs; the inspection report and the consent display carry every requested capability with its parameters and reason.
It is an npm packaging fact: generated JavaScript files import zod at run time, so the package manifest must declare it. Go has no package manifest of run-time imports and no generated Typert faces.

The first half disappears: no inspect query needs a responding page, because every provider lives in the host. The second half is kept: harness_inspect cannot invoke a service, change configuration or run code.
justification: Read-only inspection is a deliberate property, not a gap: a tool that shows the composition must not be a second way to change it, so changes go through settings forms and plugin management, each with its own approval and audit (DH-ADR-EXT-9).

reason: The Entries provider reads area A18's inventory, which lists loader entries with their supplying layer and also presets, so an entry that is mounted only inside a preset is listed; a test asserts a preset-only entry appears.

Every change to a plugin's state, including one that starts or stops nothing, replaces its descriptor and dispatches plugin.StateChanged, and the page is rendered by the host from descriptors, so an open page cannot hold rows the host no longer has.

A pending attach is one consent item whose display is the full inspection report, and its descriptor exists in state waiting-grant from the moment the request is made, so there is no row that can be answered but lacks the data to operate it.
A row is rendered from the host's descriptor, which carries its labels through every state from the request onwards; there is no client-side fold that waits for a registry read.
A render failure of a loaded browser half is a React client event; the Go design loads nothing into a page, so there is no page-local crash to show or relay.
Whether a plugin is running is one fact held by the host and shown to every browser tab alike; no tab loads code of its own, so no tab can fail where another succeeded.
The consent for an attach is an item in area A17's interaction registry, which only the channel bound to the asking agent may settle and only as an owner; the frame-wide rule is not carried over.

An attach is recorded by its own durable event, plugin-host/attached, which holds the whole value including title, version and digest; the transcript notice is rendered from that event and not from the arguments of an earlier tool call that may have left the window.

The Go harness exposes a changed tool, harness_inspect, with the same two-step shape (no argument lists providers, a query reads one). The platform argument and the client providers are gone, and the providers are Entries, Config, Tools, Events, Plugins, PluginProtocol and Runtime.
The typed notify key plugin.StateChanged carries a value copy of the plugin's descriptor when its status becomes running; listeners cannot hold up the supervisor, which is why emit becomes notify.

The same key, plugin.StateChanged, carries the descriptor with a stopped status (closed, disabled, failed) or announces its removal; a durable plugin-host/detached event records it for an attached plugin.

No event of this area is needed: a request to attach a plugin is a pending consent item in area A17's interaction registry, delivered by the registry to the bound answerer with the inspection report as its display.
The interaction registry's own settlement notice tells every view that the consent item is no longer answerable; this area adds no event of its own.

The event asks a browser page to answer an inspect query from client-side providers; every Go inspect provider lives in the host and is called directly, and there is no client plugin runtime to describe.
The event tells pages that a client inspect query settled; with no page-side providers there is no cross-page query to settle.

The two fields are replaced by the Go structs host.Config (limits, deadlines, restart budget, whether model-authored plugins may be attached) and plugin.Entry (directory, digest, grants, credential mapping). vmTimeoutMs becomes the start-up and call deadlines of a process; clientInspectTimeoutMs has no successor because no inspect query crosses to a page.

ctx.cordisInspect becomes the service key inspect.Key with the interface inspect.Service (Register as an effect, List, Query); the client manifest mirror and the client query round trip are not carried over.

ctx.dynamicCordisRunner becomes the service key plugin.Key with the interface plugin.Service (Inspect, Plugins, Run, Attach, Detach, Restart); define, run, stop and undefine of source text and every browser-facing remote method have no counterpart.

title: No code is loaded into the host or the page: a plugin is a directory and a process
The manifest is one strict JSON file with an argument-list start command
A grant binds to exact bytes: a digest and an approved copy
Protocol version 1 is shaped like MCP: lists are pulled, changes are announced, versions are integers
Version 1 offers tools, nested tool calls, committed events, plugin records and skills; every contribution is an effect of the plugin's fiber
Capabilities are a closed table checked on every inbound message; a change of grants is a restart
One supervision mechanism: the MCP fleet's rules, and tool-only plugins are fleet entries
A grant given inside a session ends with it; a standing grant comes only from an owner through the management surface
Inspection is host-only, read-only and generated
A plugin runs read-only with one state directory and no network unless granted; an unenforceable effect is shown and recorded, never assumed
A plugin directory is read, checked, digested and copied before anything runs
The plugin protocol, version 1, with a conformance kit (shared piece)
A plugin can do only what was granted: the capability table, the gate and the grant record (shared piece)
A plugin process is started confined, watched, restarted within a budget and stopped as a tree
A plugin's tools and nested calls belong to its fiber and pass the host's own paths
A tool-only plugin that speaks MCP runs as an entry of the MCP fleet
The model can write a plugin and have it attached to its own session after an owner consents
The model and the operator can inspect the composed harness and its plugins, read-only
A plugin's event subscriptions, records and skills belong to its fiber
Every invalid manifest is refused with all its problems and positions; platform, version range and protocol versions are checked
The digest is stable across systems and changes with any byte; escaping links and oversize directories are refused; a failed copy leaves nothing and a tampered copy is detected
Handshake order, version negotiation, identity check and readiness over in-memory pipes; the derived protocol schema equals the committed one
Every plugin-to-host method without its grant, or outside its parameters, is denied; a method with no table row cannot be dispatched
No plugin message can answer an interaction, create a session grant, switch a preset or reveal a secret; a mapped credential reaches only the child's environment
Hang, flood, crash and ignored shutdown each end in the stop ladder; backoff, budget, closed and stopping-unconfirmed behave as specified on a virtual clock
On a crash a sent call reports outcome unknown, an unsent one says so, nothing is replayed, and the host and other plugins continue
Disabling a plugin's loader entry leaves no tool, listener, skill provider, fleet entry or process; a grant edit restarts only that entry
A plugin tool passes validation, policy, approval and bounding in the pipeline; a nested call is logged under its parent and refused outside a served call
Only granted event types are delivered, after commit and in order; a slow plugin gets a gap notice and never delays a session; record ownership is set by the host
Attach fails closed without an answerer, logs attached before starting, cleans up on failure, ends with the agent and is not restored on resume
The inspect provider directory is golden, Entries names layers and preset-only entries, Config returns shapes only, and no provider method mutates
An MCP-protocol manifest becomes a read-only fleet entry named by the plugin id and leaves with the plugin's fiber
The policy request is read-only with one write root on the host key; network needs a grant; an unenforceable effect must be accepted in the grant or the start is refused
A real plugin from a local directory is inspected, granted, confined and limited to its grants
A plugin that crashes, hangs or refuses to stop never takes the host with it
The model writes a plugin, an owner consents in a real browser, and a later edit does not run
An MCP server packaged as a plugin directory runs through the fleet under the plugin's grant
